value.name: Greek Week: Service Project
value.description:
This year's Greek Week service project, in partnership with the Lindy Center, Dornsife Center and University & Community Partnerships, seeks to support elementary-age students in K-3 years. Students in nearby elementary schools will receive a packet of materials to aid in their reading and literacy development over the summer months, reducing "Summer Slide."

"Summer Slide" refers to the loss of knowledge in reading and math over summer break, which can lead to a snowball effect of skill loss each year. For fraternities and sororities, founded as literary societies, literacy and educational attainment are at the core of what we do! Fraternity & Sorority members will compile materials and pack the kits to be donated to the local schools.

The event will feature a mix of interactive activities including trivia, team-based debates, and Jeopardy-style games, all designed to challenge participants’ knowledge, quick thinking, and communication skills. Students will be placed in mixed teams to encourage connection and collaboration, creating a dynamic and engaging environment that blends intellectual competition with social interaction. The event will conclude with networking, photos, and a relaxed closing to celebrate participation and strengthen relationships across both communities.

value.name: Getting Started in Medical Student Research: Library Resources & Research Basics
value.description:
These two sessions, led by Sarah Hughes, Health Sciences Librarian with Drexel University Libraries, will introduce medical students to library resources and foundational research skills. Topics will include getting started with research, developing a research question, understanding different types of projects such as literature reviews, scoping reviews, and systematic reviews, choosing appropriate databases, building a search strategy, and using concepts such as MeSH terms, PICO, and PRISMA.

The sessions will also include time for questions and discussion. This event is especially intended for students interested in beginning or strengthening research projects over the summer, but all DUCOM students are welcome to attend.

Being aware of your surroundings and recognizing situations that are potentially dangerous are key to keeping yourself safe. There are measures students can take to prevent themselves from being victims of a crime. Drexel's Department of Public Safety will provide tips to encourage students to think and act accordingly—not to be scared, but to be prepared.

Light lunch will be provided for students who RSVPed on DragonLink.

value.description:
We are proud to celebrate the incredible journeys of our graduating seniors — and the cultures, stories, and communities that have shaped them. This year, we invite you to join the entire Drexel community as we celebrate your unique experiences and your time as a Dragon!  

This exciting event will feature music, food, complimentary headshots, and meaningful moments to honor our Drexel seniors. Graduates can connect with family, friends, and enjoy festivities as we celebrate Drexel's Class of 2026.

Students will be able to pick up stoles and cords honoring their various communities during this celebratory event: Kente stoles, Sarape stoles, APIM woven stoles & rainbow cords. For additional information regarding first generation cords, Spiritual and Religious Life pins, and veterans' cords, students should reach out to inclusion@drexel.edu.
